To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

compost and inorganic metal immobilising amendments can be used to reduce phytotoxicity of a contaminated soil, and that the combination of compost and inorganic amendments is more effective than either of the treatments alone.

the addition of compost and/or cyclonic ashes and/or steel shots to an industrially contaminated sandy soil reduced phytotoxic effects, increased the number of spontaneously colonizing plant species and reduced metal accumulation in plant roots.

the combined use of compost and inorganic amendments is a promising approach for phytostabilizing a metal contaminated sandy industrial soil, and that a 3 year field study is needed to assess its long-term efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phytoremediation of a metal contaminated industrial soil in Flanders, Belgium, using compost and/or inorganical metal immobilizing amendments as amendments.
the phytoremediation of metal contaminated soils.
the development of a sustainable phytostabilisation technology for the remediation of contaminated soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of compost and/or cyclonic ashes in combination with steel shots to the contaminated Overpels soil is an effective treatment for amendment assisted phyto- and biostabilization of metals in the soil.

compost addition to a metal contaminated soil reduced metal availability to plants, but did not reduce the metal concentration in the soil solution, and therefore, is not a good amendment to use in phytostabilisation of metal contaminated soils.

the combination of C with CA and SS, as well as the application of C and CA, were beneficial to phytostabilize the Overpelt soil and that the addition of C and/or CA alone was insufficient to reduce metal availability to plants to levels that would allow for spontaneous plant colonization of the contaminated soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

compost and/or inorganics are effective in reducing phytotoxicity of a contaminated sandy soil and that the combined use of compost and inorganic amendments is more effective than compost alone or inorganic amendments alone, and that the use of inorganic amendments alone is more effective than the use of compost alone.
compost addition to the Overpelt soil reduced phytotoxic metal concentrations and improved plant establishment, whereas inorganic amendments reduced metal availability for plants.
the combination of compost and inorganic amendments is a promising approach to phytostabilize contaminated soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of compost and/or metal immobilizing amendments in combination with plants may be a suitable approach for the remediation of metal contaminated soils.
the combined use of compost and/or metal immobilizing inorganic amendments can reduce metal bioavailability in soils and reduce metal accumulation in plants.
the use of a compost-based amendment in combination with inorganic amendments may be beneficial to the establishment of plant communities on contaminated soils.
